consensus_summary: Primary symbolic meaning of field is the world (sphere of humanity where the kingdom is sown and good/evil grow until harvest), fixed by Jesus’ explicit gloss in Matthew 13:38; secondary common senses include mission/harvest field, God’s cultivated people/church, and (by conflation) the soils/hearts of the sower parable.
book_summary: The world, sown with the word and reaped at harvest; its edge feeds the poor and stranger, and its hidden treasure lies beneath the surface.
boundary_disagreement: None on the primary referent; book merely layers compatible allusions (gleaning margins from Lev 19; treasure from Matt 13:44) already present as minority or adjacent notes in the consensus.
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both identify field as the world on the strength of Matt 13:38. Additional book phrases simply restate the parable’s sowing/harvest framework and attach two further scriptural associations that do not replace or restrict the shared referent; differences are therefore wording and supplementary detail, not a change of extension or category.
strongest_objection: The Levitical edge-for-the-poor detail and the hidden-treasure clause, while biblically real, are not part of the controlling dominical definition and could be viewed as ornamental rather than definitional.
